A.B. Spellman has led a distinguished career as a poet, essayist, arts advocate, and jazz enthusiast. His works include The Beautiful Days, Four Lives in the Bebop Business, and Things I Must Have Known, for which he received the NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Literary Work and Poetry.
A.B. was interviewed via Zoom on January 19, 2022 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and I’m very pleased to have A.B. Spellman with me today, who is a poet, an essayist, a jazz writer, arts advocate, teacher, and a man who hitchhiked from D.C. to New York to hear Cecil Taylor play the piano. That takes some commitment.
Not when you’re twenty years old. When you’re twenty years old all these things are easy. “Let’s go to New York, let’s hitchhike.” You know?
Yeah. What was it about his music that caused you to do that?
